title: Isolation, culture, and cryosectioning of primary porcine retinal pigment epithelium on transwell cell culture inserts
protocol: Prepare eyes for dissection.
Carefully remove excess tissue surrounding the eye globe using scissors.
Trim optic nerve back to sclera without puncturing eye globe.
Thoroughly disinfect outside of eye with PVP solution.
Place globe in a Petri dish.
Work through steps in groups of 6 while leaving the remaining eyes on ice.
Remove extra-ocular tissues and optic nerves from the first batch of 6 eyes.
Pierce the globe approximately 0.5 cm posterior to the limbus using a #10 blade scalpel.
Cut around the circumference of the globe, maintaining 0.5 cm distance from limbus.
Remove the anterior chamber (cornea and iris).
Carefully remove and discard the vitreous humor using curved tip forceps.
Gently puncture the neural retina near the optic nerve head.
Remove the neural retina with curved tip forceps, being careful not to disrupt the RPE below.
Slide the tips of the forceps underneath the retina.
Slowly lift the retina away from the underlying RPE.
Peel the retina gently to detach it with minimal damage to the RPE below.
Prepare to harvest RPE once it is exposed.
Place each globe into a well of a sterile 6-well plate.
Fill each eye cup with L-15 media (20°C–25°C, 4–5 mL per globe).
Place the 6-well plate containing globes filled with L-15 media into an incubator (37°C, 5% CO2).
Repeat steps a-c for remaining eyes.
Prepare fresh 0.25% trypsin in L-15 media (20°C–25°C) and sterilize using a 0.22 μm bottle top filter.
Remove L-15 media from eye cups with a pipette.
Replace the removed media with 0.25% trypsin in L-15 media (about 4 mL per eye).
Aspirate L-15 media to remove any remaining retinal tissue.
Incubate each plate for 45 min at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Retrieve each 6-well plate and place in a biosafety cabinet.
Triturate gently with a P1000 pipette to loosen RPE cells from the walls of each eye cup.
Transfer trypsinization media containing dislodged RPE cells into a 50 mL conical tube.
Add 4 mL fresh trypsinization media (0.25% trypsin in L-15 media) to each globe.
Return the 6-well plate to the incubator.
Centrifuge recovered media from step 4d at 400–500×g for 20 min.
Resuspend all pellets in 2 mL of fresh L-15 media and set aside at 20°C–25°C.
Place Primary RPE Culture Medium in a 37°C water bath to warm.
Retrieve each 6-well plate after the 45-min incubation period.
Incubate each plate for an additional 45 min (37°C, 5% CO2).
Use a P1000 pipette to gently pipette the trypsinization media up and down.
Retrieve the loosened RPE cells from each eye cup and collect them in a 50 mL conical tube.
Discard the used eye cups and 6-well plate into biohazardous waste.
Repeat steps using remaining 6 well plates.
Centrifuge recovered media at 400–500×g for 20 min.
Prepare 1 mL of DNaseI Stock Solution in L-15 media in a 15-mL conical tube or Eppendorf tube.
Sterile filter the prepared solution and set aside at 20°C–25°C for future use.
In two 50 mL conical tubes, prepare two 30 mL 40% Percoll cushions.
Resuspend all 4 pellets from Step 4k in 2 mL of fresh L-15 media.
Add the resuspended pellets to recovered RPE from the previous centrifugation step in a 50 mL conical tube.
Dilute the RPE suspension to 9 mL total using L-15 media (20°C–25°C).
Add 1 mL of DNaseI Stock Solution to the RPE suspension.
Mix well by gentle inversion of the tube.
Incubate for 2 min at 20°C–25°C.
Dilute the RPE suspension to 40 mL using L-15 media (20°C–25°C).
Carefully layer 20 mL of RPE suspension on top of each of the 30 mL Percoll cushions.
Centrifuge at 500×g for 3 min.
Resuspend pellets at a density of 100,000 cells per mL in prewarmed Primary RPE Culture Medium.
Add 0.25 mL of resuspended cells to the upper chamber of each well for 24-well plates.
Add 0.8 mL of prewarmed Primary RPE Culture Medium to the lower chamber for 24-well plates.
Add 0.5 mL of resuspended cells to the upper chamber of each well for 12-well plates.
Add 1.0 mL of prewarmed Primary RPE Culture Medium to the lower chamber for 12-well plates.
Add 1.5 mL of resuspended cells to the upper chamber of each well for 6-well plates.
Add 2.0 mL of prewarmed Primary RPE Culture Medium to the lower chamber for 6-well plates.
Place freshly plated RPE in an incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Change 100% of media in top and bottom wells 36-48 hours after isolation using fresh, prewarmed Primary RPE Culture Medium.
Use the same media volumes as initially added for the first media change.
Do not move plates until their first media change to avoid cells gathering in the center of the well.
Maintain primary RPE for up to 8 months with complete media changes every 3-5 days after the initial change.
Remove cell culture media from transwell membranes.
Gently wash upper and lower chambers of the transwell membrane with PBS.
Fix cells on the transwell membrane for 30 min at 20°C–25°C by adding 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) to both chambers.
Remove PFA and wash twice with PBS.
Using a #10 blade scalpel, gently cut the transwell membrane from the well around the edge to remove the membrane from the plastic.
Cut the membrane in half using curved tip forceps and small scissors to provide a flat edge for cryosectioning.
Cryoprotect tissue using 10% sucrose solution for 30 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Switch to 20% sucrose solution, maintaining the same temperature range, for another 30 minutes.
Place the membrane in a 30% sucrose solution overnight at 4°C.
Embed the membrane and prepare the block in Optimal Cutting Temperature (OCT) media in an appropriately sized embedding mold.
Allow the OCT block to freeze on dry ice.
Place a layer of OCT into an empty mold, minimizing bubbles.
Position the transwell membrane cell side down onto the OCT layer, aligning the flat edge of the membrane with the edge of the mold.
Apply additional OCT on top of the membrane to ensure it is centered in the block when frozen.
Remove the embedded membrane from the mold after freezing.
Mount the membrane into a cryostat so that it is oriented vertically and perpendicular to the blade.
Begin sectioning through the block at a thickness of 5–10 μm using slow, steady movements.
Pull down the section with a very fine-tipped paintbrush while continuing to move the block downward on the blade.
Stop sectioning after the blade has passed through the membrane but before reaching the edge of the OCT block.
Reverse the direction of the block and remove it from the blade.
Using the paintbrush, press the section back onto the surface of the block.
Retrieve section by gently pressing Superfrost Plus Microscope Slide directly to section on block.
Finish advancing the blade through the block before starting a new section.
Repeat the process through the block as necessary.
Perform immunofluorescence using standard protocols.
Perform histochemistry using standard protocols.
Perform end point histology using standard protocols.
